story_text.value:
Hi HN!

In my day to day, I switch between my Windows PC and Macbook often. One thing I find annoying is having to change what keyboard shortcuts I use depending on the OS (e.g. cmd+c vs ctrl+c for copying). It confuses my muscle memory and slows me down.

I first tried using AutoHotkey to bind MacOS-like shortcuts to Windows shortcuts. This worked, but it was hard to configure. I would also have to quit AutoHotkey to get past Anti-Cheat software on some games.

So I decided to create this app in case others also face the same issues as me.

Disclaimer: I built this app using Claude Code. I don't have much experience building windows apps so it would've been difficult to make this on my own.

story_text.value:
I have been working on Rashomon, an open-source execution recorder for AI coding agents.

The basic idea is that the agent transcript is not ground truth. Rashomon keeps its own record of what happened and compares it against the agent’s account.

For Claude Code, it records things like:

* shell commands, exit codes, and whether they may have written files * tool calls and outcomes * test commands and their outcomes * subagent lifecycle and ordering * timestamps and parent/child relationships * keyed digests of command/tool inputs and working directories

It builds a timeline from these events. It does not store prompts, responses, file contents, or tool output.

For example, it now detects patterns like:

`test fails → only test files change → same test passes`

and:

`test command fails → same command passes → no corresponding file edit`

These can indicate that an agent changed a test instead of fixing the underlying issue.

Rashomon currently runs as a Claude Code plugin or through the CLI.

CLI:

`rashomon watch`

then:

`rashomon report`

Plugin:

`/rashomon:report`

There are still edge cases around cwd, git state, test-selection arguments, generated files, retries, and parallel execution. I would be interested in feedback from people building agents on what execution signals you would want Rashomon to capture or correlate.

GitHub: https://github.com/altrace-dev-role/rashomon

title.value: Show HN: Rashomon – An independent execution record for AI coding agents

story_text.value:
Spent the weekend turning small LLMs into decision models, with some good results and a lot of learnings along the way. Topping the decision index leaderbard for their categories https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-ind...

Sharing two of them: a sub-1B model and a 4B model, both Qwen3.5 fine-tunes. When evaluated on the decision Index shared last week, the 0.8b tops the sub-1B category, 45.7% above the best other Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tune on the leaderboard. and the 4b comes in second in the 3–6B class.

Most of work was data calibration, finding external datasets and readapting them towards this scenario, so i expect a lot of improvements and work like this to come from community and push these numbers even higher. Even more if we get qwen 3.8 releases for these model categories.

story_text.value:
Hey HN,

Today, we're launching selfbench.dev, an open-source tool that lets you create and run evals automatically from your PRs.

Every benchmark with sufficient trust eventually gets benchmaxxed (Goodhart's law) - the labs are incentivized to maximize their scores on that benchmark, which isn't predictive on whether it'll actually work within your setup. This has been a time-consuming process that only the largest companies can afford to do, so we built self-bench to fix this.

Self-bench uses agents to author / review Harbor environments generated from your PRs. You then approve every eval that the agent created, and can model/harness evals concurrently on sandboxes.

To save you money, we also allow you to connect your OpenAI and Claude subscriptions so you don't have to pay raw token costs.

We ran evals on several large codebases like

- Posthog (https://selfbench.dev/PostHog/posthog)

- Next.js (https://selfbench.dev/vercel/next.js)

- Sentry (https://selfbench.dev/getsentry/sentry)

- Pi (https://selfbench.dev/earendil-works/pi)

- as well as other fantastic open-source projects (all on selfbench.dev)

From our evals:

- Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 are almost always more expensive, yet less performant than models like GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5, due to token efficiency.

- GPT-6 Luna is almost always the most effective "cost-efficient" model we've tested, not open-source models.

We'd love for you to try this on your codebase and let us know what you think!

title.value: Show HN: Self-bench – benchmark coding agents on real-world software

story_text.value:
I published it to playgama, but first want to say how it helped me. One of my ideas was to make something like X-Com but provide an indirect control - you control the leader, and your squad members make the turns themselves, based on their intelligence stats! If they get alive over battles - they learn how to play smarter, not just to get MORE hp!

Now the most interesting part - the development. I used three.js and vanilla js, no engines or frameworks at all. The critical part was to get the story, organize self testing process - game is challenging, units are clear, gameplay brings joy, no UI mistakes, etc. Other important part was to use subagents which focus on different tasks, AI downloaded the blender and music generator and provided enough of cool features to the game.

I am really proud of what I can achieve in 2-3 days , I played it myself over 10 times and every time I was enjoying it. not AAA, but can compete with indies.

story_text.value:
We’ve all heard that Instinct raised $1 billion to bring personal AI agents to everyone.

But I think anyone can build their own Instinct for a specific group of people. You know your audience, understand what they need, and know how to reach them.

So I built an open-source version.

It can make purchases online, coordinate with other people’s agents, use a computer, connect to MCP tools, manage permissions + everything else instinct wants to do.

Here’s the stack:

- Pi, the open-source agent framework used by openclaw - Maritime for each agent’s VM and computer access (cheapest infra) - Composio for app integrations and managed Google OAuth - Inkbox for imessege + email

If you want to start selling your own personal AI agent, you can host the backend on a platform like railway/vercel (around $20 a month). Maritime handles provisioning each agent’s VM and the infrastructure behind it ($1 a month per agent)

I’m open-sourcing this so we can build on it together: add more services and tools, better permissions, different payment strategies, better prompts...

The goal is to make it easy and affordable for anyone to launch a startup selling agents so that the world isnt ruled by openai dots and meta muses

Check it out and let me know what you think!

story_text.value:
Soldstack is a site for developers to get the buy or sell value of a product mainly on Poshmark right now.

The reason I built this is because eBay sold data got locked behind a login, and Poshmark data is messy and often over a year old. So I wanted to create something that makes it easier to access this data.

When I was making this, I had to be careful with cleaning out the data. For example, if one searched nike dunk low, they would get nike dunk lows, toddler and kid's sizes (which go much cheaper), bundles, other shoes, duplicates, and high outliers. But if you average all that, the price would be inaccurate.

Things to try include the price guide, the fee calculator, which all need no sign up. The Google Sheets formula does need a signup however.

I'd love feedback on whether I should expand this to Mercari or if something looks off. Thanks!

story_text.value:
Some of the many things it offers:

    - Plan: your week with time blocks, repeating or one-off. You can skip or move a single occurrence and save week templates. External calendars show next to it, and there’s an ICS feed out.
    - Board / Todos: today as a kanban board, plus undated todos with tags, filters, attributes and links. Putting a todo on a day schedules it.
    - Weekly review: clear out stale todos and write a note on the week.
    - Notebooks: notes per subject in folders, a diary, ideas, people (birthdays, relationships, every mention of them). Those work as scopes, they can hold everything mentioned here: goals, workouts, inventory, tasks, etc.
    - Goals: numeric targets and progress logs. You can link tasks to a goal, so finishing them moves it.
    - Health: habit tracking with a heatmap, and workouts that log reps, kg and km per exercise. You can put those on a date too, log how much weight you lifted, the distance you ran, etc.
    - Inventory / Shopping: things you own with quantities and restocking. Recipes use inventory items as ingredients, and what’s missing goes to the shopping list, which you can open offline in the market to see what is missing.
    - Finance: ledgers, statement import, auto-sorting rules, bills. Also integrates with inventory prices.
    - Media: a gallery and audio recordings. You can put those on notes and tasks, or standalone.
    - Reminders: on blocks and todos. You get notifications on the mobile app or PC.
A quick add (+) wheel menu for adding any important thing with one finger movement. Everything can have tags, many things can have attributes (key value pairs) that can be used with integrations: it comes with a REST API and a MCP server; you can use any AI to talk to it through scoped tokens that allow you to keep your privacy from AI companies by only giving it access to one particular project (Notebook) and its goals, tasks, notes, inventory items etc.

It’s keyboard-driven (vim-style keys) too, and you can run it in the phone both in sync with the official / you self-hosted instance, or fully isolated (never sees the internet).
